newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Italy spending control seen short of EMU standard. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Italy spending control seen short of EMU standard. [CORRECTED 13:20 GMT]

text.p: The European Commission recommended to EU member states on Monday that they tell Italy it is falling short of the goal for a single currency and should take measures to bring its public deficit in line with Maastricht Treaty goals.

In a recommendation to be discussed by EU finance ministers later, the Commission said Italy's spending control was "insufficient", that Italy had to do much more to bring its 1998 deficit below three percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) as well as be vigilant about its 1997 deficit.

"The council notes that the (Italian) government deficit in 1996 was 6.7 percent of GDP, only 0.3 percentage points below the previous year in a framework of much lower growth than expected. Nevertheless, it considers insufficient the control of general government expenditure, which, net of interest payments, increased well above the nominal rate of growth of the economy," the recommendation said.
(Clarifies that the Commission's "insufficient" comment refers to controls on Italy's 1996 spending rather than current (1997) spending controls)

The recommendations, a copy of which were obtained by Reuters, also said Italy should replace one-off measures it has taken in 1997 to reach EMU targets with "structural measures with a permanent impact on the budget".
One EU diplomat described the recommendations as being "sharply pointed".
Under EU procedures the recommendations cannot be changed by finance ministers, who were meeting in Brussels, but only approved or rejected.
